## Criterion 5: why the warm finding closes

### Changed work, unchanged predicate

The old misses remain failed measurements on their original implementations. The original R1 **50.6 ms** earned return and **59.3 ms** same-page imported replacement were not cold entries. Subsequent profile setup misses **92.2/106.5 ms**, its instrumented **50.5 ms** miss, and the newer-lineage **51.8/78/65.6 ms** misses remain in the linked reports. I do not subtract scheduling time, relabel these samples cold or attribute their cause to host contention.

The dedicated profile completed11/12 targets, observed31 warm activations at8.1–24.3 ms, and did not reproduce a miss. Its Light reference cockpit failed to run after the documented RAF-wait timeout; HeadlessChrome156 differed from the earlier shared Chrome154. That profile was inconclusive. The newer interleaved baseline also did not reproduce a miss. Neither experiment proves the old spike's cause or a reproduced spike fixed.

There is nevertheless a material implementation change to assess now. Previously, leaving the detailed pair disposed regional meshes/buffers and returning reconstructed them from numeric recipes. `src/render/regions.ts` now suspends owners into a finite LRU; `src/render/renderer.ts` detaches their meshes and geometries from the scene. Return adds those existing handles back, applies current quality and calls `update(state)` before drawing. It does not repeat the regional factory/recipe/buffer construction. Returning parked Dart art is likewise re-shown and updated rather than reconstructed.

I independently verified the sealed author's declared comparison and reran its analysis from copies:

| Same-host interleaved trial | Warm n | Median | p95 | Maximum | >50 ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Previous reconstruction baseline |56|11.75 ms|20.2 ms|22.7 ms|0|
| Retention source941008e |56|0.25 ms|1.2 ms|3.0 ms|0|

The A/B/C paths include the composed return, refuge-to-earned imported replacement and paused cockpit replacement, in Rich and Light. These are the relevant prior path classes. The final018f8ba tint/preview changes add no regional construction to that activation path. My current-source real-RAF check also reattached prepared Basin art successfully (18.7 ms activation, including the first Dart) and later reattached the post-loss Reef/Isles pair at0.4 ms. Those isolated observations are lifecycle checks, not another acceptance timing population.

**Disposition: close ASTRA-M2A-R1-02 / SOL-M2A-R1-01 for this four-region M2-A batch.** The changed warm path removes the recurring synchronous reconstruction work, and the declared current trial satisfies the same50 ms predicate with substantial measured headroom. Closure does not require asserting an unknown historical scheduling/GC cause. It also does not establish a universal maximum on all machines or every future lifecycle path. The old failed results stay attached to the earlier source; they are not a current-source measurement failure being waived.

### Ownership, memory and state

The cap is **four total regional owners**, not four retained in addition to two detailed. Detached meshes/geometries are absent from the scene; they retain CPU/GPU buffers and sign ownership. This deliberately buys less return work with more memory. The author estimates roughly450k vertices across today's four regions, alongside the unchanged bounded numeric recipe cache (256 entries/32 MiB admission, about22.8 MB used). This is not an independently measured total driver-memory budget. Since capacity equals today's region count, the benchmark incurs no steady-state eviction; it establishes no seven-region/full-world result.

Source inspection and the passing production-factory tests cover resume-before-evict, a capacity-three LRU case, unsupported-owner disposal, current-state/depletion/import replacement, quality-on-resume, stable repeated counts, exact reconstructed geometry identity and double/terminal disposal. Numeric recipes return detached copies; no mutable GameState or disposed live geometry is cached. Sign leases release their own resources while shared cel/glass remain scene-owned. Detached owners are explicitly discarded on graphics loss because Babylon cannot rebuild buffers it no longer owns in the scene.

Parked hull retention is appropriate here: strict expedition validation permits only one Dart. Hidden hierarchies draw nothing; roster removal, null-session replacement and final disposal release them. Visible re-entry updates pose, hull type, cockpit and gauges from current state. A changed hull while remote may keep its disabled old hierarchy until next visibility; it is then replaced before draw. The carrier fixture remains a diagnostic, and this is no acceptance of a larger M2-B fleet's lifetime/memory policy.

### Idle preparation and remaining construction

`GameRenderer.prepare()` is synchronous. The app calls it at most once per idle frame, only with graphics available, visible document, no open panel, no busy/confirmation operation, canvas ready and more than250 ms since the last active frame. Errors follow the graphics-error/disposal path. Readiness and loss callbacks do not authorize resuming play.

My title check measured Canopy preparation **300.2 ms** (305.6 ms wrapped callback) and Basin **64.6 ms** (64.7 ms callback). The actual menu stayed present and later settings/import interactions succeeded. A synchronous callback cannot process an intervening click; I did not dispatch input during it and do not claim zero menu input delay. The audit also retains a4,794 ms startup longtask, first render/scene work and long SwiftShader render tasks. These are not subtracted or presented as hardware frame pacing.

Author final-source preparation was approximately282/62 ms, prepared first entry17–23 ms, and unprepared entry272–387 ms. Preparation moves construction cost to title/pause/entry-ready screens; it neither eliminates that cost nor guarantees every first visit is prepared. Starting immediately can still hitch during play. Graphics restoration, a newly seen hull or future eviction can reintroduce construction even when recipes are warm. Their≤50 ms behavior is **not established** by the56 steady warm-path samples. My actual loss test discarded the detached Reef/Isles owners, reconstructed them during paused idle time (19.7/19.5 ms), and later drew them successfully; that is one concrete lifecycle result.

I accept these disclosed costs as the authorized bounded engineering/player-experience tradeoff. There is no adopted separate first-entry/menu budget to fail here; the author's recommendation for one is not a requirement retroactively satisfied by faster warm numbers. Before expanding the world, define that budget and measure resident memory, eviction and first-entry behavior. Time-sliced construction is a sensible later direction, not a required rewrite of this four-region batch.
